claims.text: An approach combining ab initio phonon-dispersion calculations with machine learning can accurately identify single-phase HEAs with exceptionally low phonon thermal conductivity.
The machine-learning models can use vibrational density of states and atomic mass variance as predictive inputs for phonon thermal conductivity.
The target materials are compositionally homogeneous, single-phase HEAs containing a random mixture of constituent elements.
DFT phonon calculations can provide descriptors including vibrational-mode softening, mass variance, and force-constant disorder.
Predictions and experimental validation will be performed at approximately 300 K under ambient conditions.
TDTR will measure thermal conductivity, while TEM or related microscopy will assess single-phase homogeneity.
Atomic-mass fluctuations and local strain-field variations in random HEA solid solutions scatter phonons.
Disorder-induced phonon scattering suppresses coherent phonon propagation and lowers thermal conductivity in HEAs.
Capturing vibrational-mode coupling together with mass and force-constant disorder isolates the principal contributors to strong phonon scattering.
The integrated approach will rank HEA compositions more accurately than empirical or single-parameter models.
The approach will identify HEAs whose measured phonon thermal conductivity is at least 30–50% lower than values predicted by conventional models.
Conventional prediction methods use simplified empirical models or average lattice parameters without representing full vibrational and disorder effects.
The approach is expected to work best for single-phase, compositionally stable HEAs.
The approach may have limited applicability to multiphase or nanoscale-segregated alloys.
Phase boundaries and additional scattering mechanisms can dominate thermal transport in multiphase or nanoscale-segregated alloys.
Failure to obtain measured conductivity at least 30–50% below conventional-model predictions would reject the hypothesis.
Consistent failure of the model to rank candidate HEAs in agreement with measured conductivity would reject the hypothesis.
